text:
alex: quick q — streaming client on macOS started returning 401s after I wired auth from an env file. I `export API_AUTH` from a dotfile and build `Authorization: Basic <base64>` myself. Any ideas?

mira: do a byte dump of the raw var. sometimes editors insert a tab or weird unicode. try `printf '%s' "$API_AUTH" | hexdump -C` to see bytes.

alex: wow — that shows a 0x09 (tab) right before the token. I pasted from a markdown note with soft-tabs. never thought a tab would break basic auth.

leo: tabs/newlines will absolutely change the base64. base64 of `user:pass` != base64 of `user:	pass`. quick fix: `export API_AUTH=$(echo -n "$API_AUTH" | tr -d '\t\r\n')`.

sam: also check your streaming wiring — if you re-compute the header for each chunk and one chunk has an untrimmed env, you can see intermittent 401s. set header once on connect.

alex: confirmed — trimming fixed it. `tr -d '\t\r\n'` and restarted the client, streaming came back. thanks! :tada:

mira: note for SDKs: we should defensively trim secrets loaded from envs before encoding. small helper in `devx-utils` would prevent a ton of these.

leo: +1. I'll open a tiny PR to add `normalizeSecret(s) => s.replace(/\s+/g, '')` for JS/Node helpers (and equivalent in other SDKs).

devex-bot: added internal note: "env secrets: trim whitespace and control chars before base64/basic header generation" — see https://intra.redwood/recipes/auth-quirks (archived).

alex: leaving the command I used for anyone who hits this: `export API_AUTH=$(cat .api_key | tr -d '\t\r\n')` — saved my afternoon.
